page: Amazon Web Services x8i.2xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor includes a substantial 480 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core scoring 2171.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 34.38 GB/sec. Text processing performance is highly competitive, placing in the top tier with a Geekbench text processing score of 2975.0. Multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks generally align with average mid-tier performance, showing a multi-core Geekbench score of 8429.0 and uncached read memory bandwidth of 75.1 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for matrix operations.

Given its high memory density of 16 GB per vCPU, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel compute or local NVMe storage. It is well-suited for in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, text processing pipelines, and lightweight machine learning inference using its AMX capabilities. However, the lack of local storage and a moderate 4 Gbps network baseline are trade-offs to consider for data-heavy storage-bound applications.
